scope: Proposition 5.4 (Bulk, marked, and boundary linear bounds) of the manuscript “Conformal universality of bulk Ising correlations under weak interactions” (preprints/Conformal-universality-of-bulk-Ising-correlations-under-weak-interactions-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 218 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 8a815e7845436e07), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 35. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Given ρ > 0, choose L sufficiently large and then r0 sufficiently large. In the homogeneous background space there are uniformly bounded splittings into the line Rvj and a complement such that Tj = ( L Bj 0 Dj ) , ∥Dj∥ ≤ ρ, ∥Bj∥ ≤ CL. (5.19) The coordinates in this splitting are denoted by (tj, wj). For a singleton marked source, in the even sector with d = 1 or the odd sector with d = 1/8, the scaled operator LdTj has a corresponding splitting about v (d) j with matrix ( 1 B (d) j 0 D (d) j ) , ∥D (d) j ∥ ≤ ρ, ∥B (d) j ∥ ≤ CL. (5.20) The even projections can be chosen invariant under square rotations. In a finite domain consider a boundary family: every carrier touches a fixed bounded lattice neighborhood of the physical edge. Its ordinary linear image, modulo constants, has norm at most ρ times its input norm, provided the local graph and flatness conditions of Proposition 4.6 hold on the required windows at the current scale. For free boundary conditions the family must be even; for either fixed boundary condition no parity restriction is imposed. The image is again a boundary family.
